what_happened.line: The Board of Health approved a building permit for a bedroom expansion on condition that a three-bedroom deed restriction is recorded; Evan Waters abstained.
The owner will get help from the administrative assistant with the deed restriction form, which must be signed, notarized and recorded before the permit is signed off.
A second agenda item was postponed because the applicant had not supplied the requested current water test; minutes are to be approved at the next meeting.
A former board member asked in public comment whether the property could tie into municipal sewer, noting sewer is available at the street.

why_it_matters: Bedroom count is what a septic system is sized and permitted for, so a deed restriction at three bedrooms keeps a larger room from changing the wastewater capacity the property is approved for, and it stays with the property for later owners.
The sewer question was raised in comment and not decided; whether the property could connect to municipal sewer instead of a compliant septic system is open on this record.
watch_next: Recording of the deed restriction on the property, which the minutes say must happen before the permit is signed off.
The postponed second agenda item, which waits on the applicant supplying a current water test, and the approval of these minutes at the next meeting.

meetings.headline: Board of Health granted septic variances at three properties and continued the Woodland Road request to March 15 for well information.
meetings.summary: The Board of Health, meeting remotely, heard Title 5 and local septic variance requests. It granted variances at 466 Mass Ave, 75 Roof Street and a Townsend Harbor Road property. It continued the Woodland Road request to March 15 so the well can be checked and the owner consulted. The agent also briefed the board on COVID-19 phase changes and vaccine clinics, and the board discussed moving the March 15 meeting earlier because of the town caucus.

The board took up variances at 75 Roof Street, with the new well to be a permit condition; the minutes record the vote as not audible.

310 Sunny Hill Road withdrew its groundwater offset request, and 244 Pleasant Street must return for new variances because its system type changed.

why_it_matters: Septic variances decide whether a property owner can repair or replace a failing system on a tight lot, which touches groundwater and well protection near Lake Shirley and elsewhere in town.
The Woodland Road request is still open, so its outcome depends on a well test the board has not yet seen.
watch_next: March 15 at 7:15: the Woodland Road request returns, and the board may meet earlier that evening if the town caucus falls that day.
The first April meeting: 244 Pleasant Street returns with new variance requests.
